To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined a new three‐dimensional potential energy surface for the van der Waalds interaction between argon and ammonia, and that the surface is an accurate representation of the intermolecule potential for this system.

the Ar–NH3 intermolecular potential surface has a global minimum at a center‐to‐center separation of 3 57 Å, an angle between the Ar–NH _{3} center‐of‐ mass vector and the NH _{3} symmetry axis of 96.6°, and an angle between the van der Waids bond axis and the Ar atom of 60°.
the Ar–NH3 intermolecular potential has been determined from spectroscopic data and the surface is highly anisotropic.

the intermolecular force field of Ar–NH3 is dominated by a single, very strong van der Waals interaction between the Ar atom and the H atom in the NH3 molecule.
